facts.text: Grimsley sits high on the Cumberland Plateau, with elevations between 1,700 and 1,800 feet, while its western edge drops into the 800‑foot gorge of the East Fork Obey River.
The first post office in Grimsley opened in 1902, a milestone that formally recognized the community and likely drew its name from local Grimsley families.
The Beaty General Merchandise Store, built in 1924 on State Highway 28, was listed in 2014 on the National Register of Historic Places for its early 20th‑century commerce.
Early 1800s pioneers from Virginia, North Carolina, and Kentucky settled Grimsley, attracted by timber, fertile valleys along the East Fork Obey River, and opportunities for farming and livestock.
Indian Trace and Scott’s Turnpike linked Grimsley to Jamestown and Clarkrange in the 1840s, enabling stock drives southward and boosting early commerce.
